summary: Former carnival worker Eugene Spriggs founded the Twelve Tribes in 1970s Chattanooga, a communal Christian sect that spread across the US and abroad while systematically beating children, preaching racist doctrine and using members as unpaid labor.

evidence.note: Spriggs's 1937 birth in Tennessee and early life
1972 marriage to Marsha and founding of the Vine community in Chattanooga
expansion to Island Pond, Vermont under David Jones
child-beating doctrine and the training manual laid out at length
1984 state raid in Vermont and its collapse in court
long segment on Spriggs's racist Curse of Ham theology and pro-slavery teaching
teaching that gay people deserve death; later a boy punished as gay
infant death in a whooping cough outbreak and a stillbirth after denied care
2013 undercover filming and removal of children by German authorities
unpaid member labor in cult construction firms and LLC structure
opens on the 2021 Marshall Fire that began on cult property; current status discussed

notes: Cult and founder treated as co-primary; lifetime rule sets covered_span 1937-2021. The 2021 Marshall Fire and 2023 investigation frame the opening briefly, so they set reaches_present rather than extending covered_span. France raid is a one-line mention and is left out of setting. Several US states (TN, VT, FL, CO) share the story, so no single subdivision.
